blocks.s: The straight motion, or intellective operation likened to straight motion, belongs to angels insofar as the higher angels extend themselves to the providence of the lower, and the lowest angels, passing through all things in right order, tend toward those subject to them — or, as Dionysius says: "They are moved in a straight line whenever they come forth in the providence of those subject to them, ordering all things rightly." As Thomas affirms in the Secunda Secundae (q. 180, a. 6), this straight motion in the angels is not taken as proceeding discursively from one thing to another in their knowing — for they know by simple intuition — but only according to the order of their providence, insofar as the higher illumines, teaches, and directs the lower. This operation is likened to straight motion because, just as straight motion passes from one thing to another, so in this action the angels do not return from the same to the same but proceed from themselves toward their subjects.
